e-12466.problem: The lamina $D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le x \le y  ,\, 0 \le y \le 1 \big\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y) = x^2y.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
e-12466.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
M_y = \iint\limits_D x \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda(x,y) = x^2y .$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot {x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{3}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{3}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y[{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{{y}^{4}}{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{y}^{5}}{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{6}}{24}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: The lamina $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le x,\,0\le x\le 1}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=3xy.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
after.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=3xy.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 3xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot {[{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{xy}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{1}{xy}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{x=1}^{x={e}^{y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(9-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type I plane region, as shown below.

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 4x}

$$
